9.2.1. qnav.estimation.state

9.2.1.1. state.py

summary:

Supported base estimation state classes used to hold estimated data. This module contains classes that handle the estimated state of the platform during simulations. These are shared between the employed fusion methods. Extensions of the base class are required for the handling of addition data (such as error states and kalman matrices).

authors:
Prof. Jason Ralph - jfralph@liverpool.ac.uk
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation of module.

class qnav.estimation.state.EstimatedState(ground_truth: ~qnav.waypoints.trajectory.GroundTruth, gravity_model: ~qnav.gravity.base.GravityModel = <qnav.gravity.simple.SimpleUniform object>)[source]

The base estimated state holding only general state information. Simply maintains the estimated time, position, velocity, acceleration, attitude and angle rates of the platform. Additionally, this also holds a shared gravity model for calculating the expected gravity dynamics.

property timestamp: float

Returns the current estimated duration of the simulation (in seconds).

Returns:

The estimated time (in seconds).

Return type:

float

property position: ndarray

Returns the estimated position (in degrees-degrees-metres). This is the estimated position represented by an array of latitude, longitude and altitude values respectively.

Returns:

The estimated position (in degrees-degrees-metres).

Return type:

np.ndarray

property velocity: ndarray

Returns the estimated velocity (in meters/second). This is the estimated velocity in body axis represented as an array of along, across and down velocities respectively.

Returns:

The estimated velocity (in meters/second).

Return type:

np.ndarray

property acceleration: ndarray

Returns the estimated acceleration (in meters/second^2). This is the estimated acceleration in body axis represented as an array of along, across and down accelerations respectively.

Returns:

The estimated acceleration (in meters/second^2).

Return type:

np.ndarray

property attitude: ndarray

Returns the estimated attitude (in degrees). This is the estimated attitude in NED axis represented as an array of heading, pitch and yaw angles respectively.

Returns:

The estimated attitude (in degrees).

Return type:

np.ndarray

property angle_rates: ndarray

Returns the estimated angle rates (in degrees/second). This is the estimated angle rates in body axis represented as an array of P, Q and R euler angles respectively.

Returns:

The estimated angle rates (in degrees/second).

Return type:

np.ndarray

property gravity_model: GravityModel

Returns the shared gravity model. This is the gravity model instance used for estimating the gravitational effect during estimation and fusion. For consistency, this is held in the estimated state so it is shared.

Returns:

The estimation gravity model.

Return type:

GravityModel

update_estimates(timestamp: float = None, position: ndarray = None, velocity: ndarray = None, acceleration: ndarray = None, attitude: ndarray = None, angle_rates: ndarray = None)[source]

Overwrites selected current estimated states. This is namely used when estimation fusion is applied and the internal states must be updated. To prevent accidental overwriting of estimated states or the setting of invalid data, all changes must be submitted through this method.

Parameters:

  • timestamp (float) – The updated timestamp marking the estimated current duration of the simulation (in seconds).

  • position (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated position vector containing the latitude (in degrees), longitude (in degrees) and altitude (in metres) respectively.

  • velocity (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated velocity vector for the North, East and Down components respectively (in m/s).

  • acceleration (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated acceleration vector for the North, East and Down components respectively (in m/s^2).

  • attitude (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated attitude vector for the Heading, Pitch and Roll components respectively (in degrees).

  • angle_rates (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated angle rate vector for the P, Q and R body rates respectively (in deg/s).

as_dict() → dict[str, float | ndarray][source]

object>)[source]

Extended estimation state featuring Kalman Filter properties. This is an extension for the standard estimated state so that Kalman states can also be represented. These additions include shared Kalman Filter matrices and state errors.

property state_vector

Returns estimated states in form of state vector. A commonly used representation of estimated states in Kalman Filters.

Returns:

Kalman State Vector

Return type:

numpy.ndarray (15-elements)

update_estimates(timestamp: float = None, position: ndarray = None, velocity: ndarray = None, acceleration: ndarray = None, attitude: ndarray = None, angle_rates: ndarray = None, state_errors: ndarray = None)[source]

Overwrites selected current estimated states. This is namely used when estimation fusion is applied and the internal states must be updated. To prevent accidental overwriting of estimated states or the setting of invalid data, all changes must be submitted through this method.

Parameters:

  • timestamp (float) – The updated timestamp marking the estimated current duration of the simulation (in seconds).

  • position (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated position vector containing the latitude (in degrees), longitude (in degrees) and altitude (in metres) respectively.

  • velocity (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated velocity vector for the North, East and Down components respectively (in m/s).

  • acceleration (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated acceleration vector for the North, East and Down components respectively (in m/s^2).

  • attitude (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated attitude vector for the Heading, Pitch and Roll components respectively (in degrees).

  • angle_rates (numpy.ndarray (3-elements)) – The updated angle rate vector for the P, Q and R body rates respectively (in deg/s).

  • state_errors (numpy.ndarray (15-by-15 elements)) – The update Kalman state errors.
